title: The Buzzing Postman: How a Bee Delivers a Plant's Future
title_zh: 嗡嗡作响的邮差：蜜蜂如何递送植物的未来
intro_zh: 本文约550词，共8段，含6个CET-4核心词，句子难度中等，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: Every February, a strange traffic jam appears on the highways of California. Trucks loaded with wooden boxes drive north through the night, and inside each box are about ten thousand honeybees. The destination is the almond orchards, where billions of pink flowers open at almost the same moment. The bees have not come for a holiday. They have come to work, and the three-billion-dollar almond harvest depends on how well they do it.
paragraphs.zh: 每年二月，加利福尼亚的高速公路上都会出现一种奇怪的堵车。装满木箱的卡车彻夜向北行驶，每个箱子里大约装着一万只蜜蜂。它们的目的地是杏树果园，那里有数十亿朵粉色的花几乎在同一时刻开放。蜜蜂不是来度假的。它们是来工作的，而价值三十亿美元的杏子收成，取决于它们干得有多好。

paragraphs.en: A plant has a problem that people rarely think about: it cannot move. Its male cells must reach a female cell that may sit only a few centimetres away, which for a rooted organism is a long journey. Wind can carry dust-like pollen, and many trees do use wind. But wind is wasteful: it throws millions of grains into the air in the hope that a few will land in the right place. An animal, by contrast, makes the delivery personal.
paragraphs.zh: 植物有一个人们很少想到的难题：它不能移动。它的雄性细胞必须抵达一个可能只有几厘米远的雌性细胞，而对一个扎根不动的生物来说，这是一段漫长的旅程。风可以携带尘埃般的花粉，许多树木也确实靠风传粉。但风很浪费：它把数以百万计的花粉粒抛向空中，指望有少数能落在正确的地方。相比之下，动物能把这场投递变成“专人送达”。

paragraphs.en: A bee's body is a delivery tool. Its head and legs are covered with branched hairs that hold grains the way a comb holds dust. As the bee pushes into a flower to reach the sweet liquid at its base, grains attach to her back; a few seconds later, at the next flower, the same movement transfers them to exactly the right spot. One honeybee may visit fifty to a hundred flowers on a single trip, and a strong colony makes twenty thousand trips a day.
paragraphs.zh: 蜜蜂的身体本身就是一件投递工具。它的头和腿上长满分叉的绒毛，像梳子夹住灰尘一样夹住花粉粒。当蜜蜂钻进花朵去够花心的甜液时，花粉粒便粘在它的背上；几秒钟后，在下一朵花上，同样的动作又把花粉送到恰到好处的位置。一只蜜蜂一趟可能造访五十到一百朵花，而一个强壮的蜂群一天能完成两万次这样的出勤。

paragraphs.en: Some flowers go further and lock their pollen inside narrow tubes. Only a violent shake will release it. Bumblebees solve this puzzle by holding the flower and vibrating their flight muscles about 400 times a second — a sound you can actually hear. Tomato, potato and blueberry growers value bumblebees partly for this trick, which honeybees cannot perform well.
paragraphs.zh: 有些花更进一步，把花粉锁在狭窄的管子里，只有剧烈的震动才能让它释放出来。熊蜂解开了这个难题：它们抱住花朵，让飞行肌每秒振动约四百次——那声音你其实听得见。番茄、土豆和蓝莓的种植者之所以看重熊蜂，部分原因正是这项本领，而蜜蜂做不好这件事。

paragraphs.en: There is an invisible partner in this work: electricity. A flower carries a weak negative charge, while a bee in flight builds up a positive one, so as she approaches, the difference literally pulls pollen grains through the air onto her body. Researchers at Bristol University found that a flower's charge may even change after a visit, perhaps signalling that it has already been served.
paragraphs.zh: 这项工作还有一位看不见的伙伴：电。花朵带有微弱的负电荷，而飞行中的蜜蜂会积累正电荷，因此当它靠近时，这种电位差真的会把花粉粒隔着空气吸到它身上。布里斯托大学的研究者发现，花朵的电荷在一次造访之后甚至会发生变化，也许是在发出“我已经被服务过了”的信号。

paragraphs.en: The result is our dinner. Roughly one third of the food we eat — apples, cucumbers, coffee, chocolate, pumpkins — relies on animals to move pollen from one plant to another. Yet in some parts of China, pear and apple farmers now pollinate their trees by hand with a brush or a feather tied to a long stick, because so few wild bees are left.
paragraphs.zh: 结果就是我们的晚餐。我们所吃的食物中大约有三分之一——苹果、黄瓜、咖啡、巧克力、南瓜——依靠动物把花粉从一株植物搬到另一株植物。然而在中国的一些地方，梨农和果农如今要用刷子或绑在长杆上的羽毛为树人工授粉，因为野蜂已经所剩无几。

paragraphs.en: That is the quiet decline scientists keep warning about: heavy pesticide use, huge fields of a single crop, and disease have cut wild bee numbers in many regions. Still, the news is not all alarm. City gardens, roadside strips and rooftop hives turn out to be surprisingly good habitats, sometimes richer than the farmland around them.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是科学家不断警告的那种悄然的下降：农药的大量使用、单一作物的大片农田以及疾病，已经让许多地区的野蜂数量减少。不过，消息并不全是坏消息。城市花园、路边的绿化带和屋顶蜂箱竟然是出人意料的好栖息地，有时比周围的农田还要丰富。

paragraphs.en: You do not need a hive to help. A small garden with flowers of several colours, a few untidy corners left uncut, and no spraying in the middle of the day will welcome more bees than a neat empty lawn ever could. The almond trucks will keep rolling north each winter. But the insects that need no truck at all are already on your street, waiting to be invited.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要养一箱蜂才能帮忙。一个小小的花园、几种不同颜色的花、几处不去修剪的凌乱角落，再加上中午不打药，就能比一片修剪整齐的空草坪招来更多的蜜蜂。每年冬天，那些运蜂的卡车仍会一路向北。但完全不需要卡车的昆虫，此刻就在你的街道上，等着被邀请。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why California farmers drive trucks north every February.
How bees and flowers work together to move pollen and produce food.
Why bumblebees are more useful to growers than honeybees.
How city gardens can replace farmland as bee habitats.
questions.explain: 全文围绕蜜蜂如何为植物传粉展开：从杏园运蜂、风媒的浪费、蜜蜂身体结构与静电、熊蜂的震动授粉，到传粉与食物的关系及蜂群减少，主旨是蜜蜂与花朵合作完成传粉并带来食物。A、C、D都只是文中某一细节。

questions.q: According to the passage, why is wind a wasteful way for plants to move pollen?
options: It only works for trees that grow in open fields.
It often carries grains to flowers of the wrong species.
It sends millions of grains into the air hoping a few will succeed.
It cannot lift grains that are heavy and wet.
questions.explain: 第二段明确说风媒很浪费：它把数百万粒花粉抛向空中，只指望少数落在正确的地方，故选C。文中并未说风媒只适用于开阔地的树，也没提花粉被送到错误物种或花粉过重过湿。

questions.q: What can we infer about the farmers in some parts of China who pollinate their trees by hand?
options: They are trying to grow larger fruit than their neighbours.
Wild bees in their area are too few to do the job.
Their trees belong to a kind that bees cannot pollinate.
Hand pollination costs them almost nothing.
questions.explain: 第六段说这些果农用刷子或羽毛人工授粉，原因是‘so few wild bees are left’，可推断当地野蜂太少，无法完成自然授粉，故选B。文中没有提到他们要比邻居的果子更大，也没说这类树蜜蜂无法授粉，更没说人工授粉末几乎不花钱。

questions.q: In paragraph 7, the word alarm most probably means ______.
questions.explain: 此处 alarm 是名词，用于‘the news is not all alarm’，与上文蜂群数量下降的坏消息呼应，意为‘令人担忧的事’，故选B。它并非指真正的警报声、计划突变或愤怒情绪。
